title: Denying the meeting leads to the punishment.
subtitle: The other side of the separation
then: Verse 15 described the garden. This verse completes the picture of the separation. Ibn Kathir says each will be {idea}repaid according to his deeds{/idea}. Those who {trap}denied the signs and the meeting with their Lord{/trap} are brought to the punishment.
now: Most of us do not deny the Hereafter out loud. {trap}We just live as if there is no appointment.{/trap} The late-night choices nobody sees, the unkind word you never apologized for. {idea}Living ready for the meeting is the answer to this verse{/idea}, and it starts today.
old: I believe in the Hereafter, so this verse is not about me.
new: Believing in the meeting means living like I will actually attend it.
try: Before sleeping tonight, ask yourself: if I met Allah tomorrow, what would I want to have fixed today?

title: Glorify Allah as evening falls and morning breaks.
subtitle: The day's turning points as times of praise

row.title: just a clock
sub: time to go home, time to wake

then: Ibn Kathir titles this passage the command to pray five times daily. Allah glorifies Himself and tells His servants to glorify Him at times that follow each other. {idea}Night comes with its darkness, then morning with its light{/idea}, and each change shows {reward}His might and power.{/reward}
now: You step out of the office and the streetlights are coming on. Or your alarm rings and grey light is at the curtain. {trap}You reach for your phone.{/trap} {idea}The verse offers a different first move: glorify the One who turned the day.{/idea}
old: Evening and morning are just when my day starts and ends.
new: Every evening and morning are invitations to remember Allah.
try: Tomorrow, before you check your phone, say Subhan Allah three times.

title: All praise is His, from the darkest night to noon.
subtitle: Praise across heavens, earth, and every hour
then: Ibn Kathir says the glorifying of the previous verse is {idea}followed by fitting praise{/idea}. He is praised for all He made in the heavens and the earth. The night time named here is {trap}when darkness is deepest{/trap}, and noon {reward}is when the day is brightest.{/reward} Both are His.
now: The lunch break at noon when you eat at your desk. The late night when you cannot sleep and the house is silent. {idea}Both are moments of His making.{/idea} One sentence of praise turns a blank stretch of time into worship.
old: Praise is for special moments of blessing.
new: Every hour of the day, bright or dark, is a time to praise Him.
try: At lunch today, say Alhamdulillah before you take the first bite.

title: Life from death, death from life. So will you rise.
subtitle: Opposites that show His power
then: Ibn Kathir lists the pairs: {idea}plant from seed and seed from plant, egg from chicken and chicken from egg{/idea}, even a believer from disbelievers and a disbeliever from believers. He revives dead earth with rain. {reward}And so you will be brought out{/reward} of the earth.
now: Your uncle who never prayed now stands in the front row at Jumuah. A child from a quiet home grows into the family's light. {idea}Allah brings life from places that looked dead.{/idea} That includes a heart that feels empty, including yours.
old: Some people, maybe me, are too far gone to change.
new: The One who brings life from death can bring my heart back too.
try: Make dua for one person you have given up on, and one part of yourself you have given up on.

title: From dust, and now you spread across the earth.
subtitle: The sign that is your own existence
then: Ibn Kathir traces the stages: {idea}dust, a drop, a clot, flesh, bones{/idea}, then a soul. A small weak baby grows until he builds cities and crosses seas. He cites a hadith that Adam was made from a handful of all the earth, so {reward}his children vary as the earth varies.{/reward}
now: You sit in the airport scrolling, about to fly across continents for work. {trap}You feel capable, in control.{/trap} {idea}Every skill you have started with dust, then a helpless baby.{/idea} The verse makes your own life the sign.
old: I have earned everything I am able to do.
new: I began as dust. Every ability I have is a gift and a sign.
try: Look at your hands for a moment today and say: You made me from dust. Thank You.

title: He made spouses from yourselves, with love and mercy.
subtitle: Marriage as a sign of Allah
then: Ibn Kathir explains that out of {reward}perfect mercy{/reward} Allah made spouses from people's own kind, so there would be harmony. A man stays with a woman {idea}because he loves her, or out of compassion{/idea}, for their child, or because she needs his care. {idea}Both love and mercy keep a home.{/idea}
now: The argument over dishes again. Then your spouse brings you tea without being asked, after a long shift. {idea}That small kindness is a sign of Allah.{/idea} When love feels tired, {reward}mercy is still there to hold things together.{/reward}
old: When the spark fades, the marriage is failing.
new: Allah put both love and mercy between us. Mercy carries us when love is tired.
try: Do one small act of mercy for your spouse or a family member today, without saying why.

title: Every language and every face is His sign.
subtitle: Human variety as proof of the Creator
then: Ibn Kathir lists many languages of his time and says {idea}only Allah knows how many are spoken{/idea}. Every person has two eyes, a nose, a mouth, and yet {reward}none looks exactly like another.{/reward} Each face has something of its own.
now: On the bus you hear three languages at once. At the hospital the nurse, the doctor and the patient beside you all look different. {trap}It is easy to judge or to not notice.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to see each face as a sign.{/idea}
old: People who look or speak differently from me feel foreign.
new: Every different face and voice is a signature of the same Creator.
try: Today, notice one person who looks or speaks very differently from you. Silently say Subhan Allah.

title: Your sleep and your work are both His signs.
subtitle: Rest and earning as gifts
then: Ibn Kathir says among His signs is {reward}the cycle of sleep{/reward}, when people stop moving and rest so their exhaustion goes away. Then He lets them {idea}seek a living and travel by day{/idea}. Signs, he says, for those who listen, meaning those who understand.
now: You scroll in bed until 2am, then drag yourself to work tired and short-tempered. {trap}Sleep feels like something to cut.{/trap} {idea}The verse calls your sleep a sign{/idea}, as much as your paycheck. Rest is part of the design, not a weakness.
old: Sleep is time I lose from getting things done.
new: Sleep is a gift from Allah, and so is the strength I wake with.
try: Put your phone away 20 minutes earlier tonight, and sleep with the intention of rest He gave.

title: Lightning brings fear and hope at once.
subtitle: One flash, two feelings, and rain that revives
then: Ibn Kathir explains: sometimes you {trap}fear the heavy rain and thunderbolts{/trap}, and sometimes a flash gives {reward}hope that much-needed rain is coming{/reward}. Then water revives barren land. {idea}In that is proof of the resurrection.{/idea}
now: A storm warning pings on your phone. The farmer three villages away is praying for it, while you worry about the commute. {idea}One flash holds both fear and hope.{/idea} Your relationship with Allah needs both, like two wings.
old: Either I fear Allah, or I trust His mercy.
new: I can fear Him and hope in Him at the same time. Both keep me steady.
try: In your next dua, ask Allah to protect you from one thing and to grant you one thing.

title: Sky and earth stand by His command, until He calls.
subtitle: One call, and everyone comes out
then: Ibn Kathir notes that when 'Umar swore a strong oath he would say, {idea}No, by the One by whose command the heaven and the earth stand.{/idea} They stand firm by His command. On the Day of Resurrection, {reward}one call will bring the dead out of their graves.{/reward}
now: You stand on a balcony and the city is still there, every building upright. You take it for granted that the ground will hold tomorrow. {idea}It holds because He holds it.{/idea} And the same command will one day call you by name.
old: The world runs on its own.
new: Everything stands by Allah's command, and one day His call will raise me.
try: Next time you stand outside, look at the sky for ten seconds and remember who holds it.

title: Everyone in the heavens and earth belongs to Him.
subtitle: All submit, willingly or unwillingly
then: Ibn Kathir explains that He owns everything in the heavens and earth and all of it is in His service. {idea}All are humble before Him and submit to Him, willingly or unwillingly.{/idea} Even the one who refuses Him {trap}cannot escape His rules{/trap} of birth, aging and death.
now: Your body ages whether you agree or not. Your heart beats without your permission. {trap}In those ways you already submit.{/trap} {idea}The real question is whether you submit willingly{/idea}, with your prayer, your choices, your time.
old: I am in charge of my life.
new: I belong to Allah either way. Let me belong to Him willingly.
try: Pick one area where you resist Allah. Give it to Him willingly today in one small act.

title: Bringing you back is even easier for Him.
subtitle: The highest description belongs to Allah
then: Mujahid said, {idea}repeating it is easier for Him than originating it, and originating it is easy for Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites a hadith qudsi: the son of Adam denies Me by saying I will not remake him as I first made him. {reward}His is the highest description{/reward}: there is nothing like Him.
now: You look at an old photo of your great-grandparents and think, they are gone, dust now. {trap}The idea of them standing again feels too much.{/trap} {idea}Making them the first time was the harder part, if anything is hard for Him.{/idea}
old: Bringing people back from death seems impossible.
new: The One who made me from nothing can easily make me again.
try: Make dua today for one relative who has passed away, knowing you will meet again.

title: Would you make your servant an equal partner?
subtitle: A parable from your own life
then: The idolaters' pilgrimage chant said Allah had {trap}no partner except one He owned{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains the parable: none of you would let your own servant share your wealth equally. {idea}If you would hate that for yourself, how can you assign partners to Allah from His own creation?{/idea}
now: Imagine your employee demanding half your house and equal say in your family. You would never accept it. {trap}Yet we hand our hopes and fears to people and things Allah made.{/trap} {idea}The verse uses your own sense of fairness to show His oneness.{/idea}
old: Relying on others alongside Allah is harmless.
new: Nothing Allah created can share His place. I would not accept that for myself.
try: When you catch yourself trusting a person more than Allah today, pause and ask Him first.

title: They follow their desires without knowledge.
subtitle: When wants replace evidence

row.title: my desire
sub: I want it, so it is fine

then: After the parable, Ibn Kathir explains, Allah points out that the idolaters worshipped false gods {trap}out of their own folly{/trap}, following desires with no knowledge. {idea}No one can guide those whom Allah lets go astray{/idea}, and no one can save them from His power.
now: You want the thing, so you search until you find a voice online saying it is fine. {trap}Your desire chose the answer before you asked.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks: is this knowledge, or is it what I want dressed up as knowledge?{/idea}
old: If it feels right, it probably is.
new: Feelings are not knowledge. I need guidance, not just agreement.
try: Before your next big decision, ask: am I following knowledge or a want? Then make a quick dua for guidance.

title: Turn your face to the faith you were made for.
subtitle: The fitrah every person is born with
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {idea}created people to recognize Him{/idea}, linking it to the covenant when all souls said, yes, You are our Lord. He cites the hadith: {reward}every child is born upon the fitrah.{/reward} Most people do not know this.
now: Watch a small child look at the night sky and ask who made the stars. {idea}That question is the fitrah.{/idea} Years of noise, screens and cynicism bury it. {trap}You might feel faith is far from you.{/trap} The verse says it is the deepest part of you.
old: Faith is something I have to force myself into.
new: Faith is what I was made with. Turning to Allah is coming home.
try: Spend five quiet minutes today with no phone, just remembering Allah, and notice what feels natural.
